hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: Stealth tanker activity using transponder blackouts is lifting Hormuz flows from a trickle to a stream — the physical blockade remains formally in place but is eroding operationally, and Rystad base case now assumes a phased diplomatic reopening beginning mid-July 2026, which would structurally reduce the supply shock thesis.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: BLS confirmed May CPI at 4.2% YoY — the highest since April 2023 — driven by energy up 3.9% for the month, with core CPI at 2.9% and wage growth lagging price growth, locking in the stagflation dynamic heading into the June 17 FOMC decision.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Statista confirmed hyperscaler capex on track for $725B in 2026 with capital intensity at 45 to 57 percent of revenue, but big tech companies issued $100B of bonds in 2026 to fund AI infrastructure and investors demanded record CDS protection — the ROI validation window is compressing toward Q4 2026.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: JP Morgan describes gold as stuck between the 200-day moving average at $4,340 and the 50-day at $4,730 with central bank net purchases collapsing to just 16 tons in Q1 2026 — down from 225 tons per quarter average in prior years — and Fed hike risk from energy inflation is the key near-term headwind to price recovery.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: Goldman Sachs and Citi both raised copper price forecasts on Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula production disruptions with the ex-US deficit now estimated at 640,000 tonnes, but the US Commerce Secretary tariff recommendation due by end of June 2026 remains the binary catalyst that could either trap inventory and tighten ex-US markets further or release it in a price-destabilizing surplus flush.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: Hyperscaler capex confirmed at $725B with power bottlenecks cited as the primary constraint on US AI build-out progress — Microsoft disclosed an $80B Azure backlog it cannot fulfill due to power constraints — sustaining urgent structural demand for nuclear baseload capacity to serve data centers.

ALAB.note: Fundamental thesis remains intact — Q1 2026 GAAP operating income of $61.8M with 36.2% non-GAAP operating margin and Q2 2026 revenue guidance of $355M to $365M implies 15 to 18 percent sequential growth — but competition is intensifying with Marvell launching the Teralynx T100 102.4 Tbps AI switch silicon in June 2026 and at P/E 87 the stock is priced for continued dominance it may not retain.

POWL.note: Data center electrical equipment thesis is directly reinforced by Microsoft disclosing an $80B Azure backlog constrained by power availability — POWL as a switchgear and power distribution manufacturer sits exactly at this bottleneck — and P/E 42 is justifiable given the structural multi-year order pipeline.

MOD.note: Negative FCF of -$101M remains a direct contradiction of quality-of-earnings discipline required in a stagflation regime where cost of capital is punishing — the data center thermal management thesis is real but MOD is burning cash to capture it and there is no confirmation of inflection.

GFS.note: CHIPS Act thesis remains unvalidated with no new fabrication contract catalysts and GFS continues to trade on hope rather than booked revenue acceleration — the geopolitical reshoring narrative is sound but execution evidence is absent.

CRDO.note: CRDO delivered a decisive Q4 2026 earnings beat with EPS of $1.16 against estimates of $0.98 — an 18.37% beat — and the surge in call option volume signals institutional momentum, making CRDO the cleaner AI connectivity play with confirmed earnings velocity versus peers at similar or higher multiples.

ARM.note: ARM at P/E 111 with only $750M FCF remains priced for absolute perfection and the thesis depends entirely on royalty rate expansion and AI chip proliferation materializing faster than macro headwinds — in a higher-for-longer rate environment driven by 4.2% CPI this valuation carries unacceptable downside asymmetry.

S.note: SentinelOne has a genuine FCF improvement trajectory at $268M but the cybersecurity spend environment in a stagflation regime is bifurcating toward incumbent vendors with proven ROI and CRWD remains the dominant share-gainer — the fundamental improvement is real but the competitive moat is not yet proven at scale.

ZS.note: Zscaler with $1.1B FCF and 26% ARR growth YoY to over $3B is the strongest fundamental name in the WATCH list, but the AVOID signal reflects valuation compression risk in a higher-for-longer rate environment — the thesis has drifted from pure-play ARR growth to a value-relative-to-peers argument, which is a weaker base.

AXON.note: AXON at EV/EBITDA 379 with only $63M FCF has experienced complete thesis drift — the original law enforcement tech thesis has been overwhelmed by a valuation that requires hyper-growth compounding for a decade without any margin of safety — insider selling reported by TipRanks in early June 2026 is an additional red flag confirming the AVOID signal.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.
